sections.name: File setup, ClaimReview
sections.title: Review and fact types
sections.what: Imports the fact type and defines the shape of a reviewer's verdict: whether the claim is supported, whether the source attributes it, the exact sentence, and a reason.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes the reviewer's answer a fixed shape that the rest of the code can rely on.
sections.watch_out: Other files depend on this exact shape, so changing a field name here must be matched elsewhere.

sections.name: isAdmittedFact
sections.title: The admission test
sections.what: Returns yes only when a fact is marked verified and relevant, comes from a direct and matched source, has a statement that is a real part of its passage, and has a recorded independent review. A saved badge alone is not enough.
sections.why: Stated in the comment above it: admission depends on independent gates.
sections.watch_out: Every condition is required, so one flag set incorrectly upstream can exclude a valid fact.

sections.name: applyClaimReview
sections.title: Applying a reviewer's verdict
sections.what: Takes a fact and a reviewer's verdict, checks the verdict against the passage, and returns the fact marked verified or held out, with a reason for each gate that failed.
sections.why: Stated in the code: a positive review cannot rescue a bad source or a quote that is not in the passage.
sections.watch_out: A quote that is really in the passage can still carry the wrong meaning, and that judgement is left to the reviewer.

summary: Decides whether a research fact may be used. It must pass source, relevance and an independent literal-claim review, and a review can confirm a fact but never rescue a failed check.
purpose: The gatekeeper that moves a research fact from candidate to admitted.
why: Stated in the header: admission depends on independent gates, not on a saved badge.
how: First, the admission check requires the fact to be marked verified, relevant, from a direct and matched source, with supported meaning, an exact statement inside its passage, and a recorded review. Second, the review step takes the reviewer's verdict, checks the statement is a real piece of the passage and at least 20 characters long, checks that the structured value appears in the statement unless the field is a factual event or project overview, then marks the fact verified or held out and records the reasons.
inputs: A research fact, an optional structured value with field and value, and a reviewer verdict with supported, attributed, statement and reason.
outputs: An updated fact with its status set to verified or held out, the statement kept or cleared, its semantic result recorded, and reasons appended. The admission check returns yes or no.
risks: A reviewer statement that is a true piece of the passage but misleading can still be admitted. The value check is skipped for factual events and overviews. Attribution failure also marks the fact as not relevant.
debug: Read the reasons list on the fact's assessment. It names the failed gate, such as the statement not being in the passage or the value being absent. Check the semantic review version number and look for whitespace differences between the statement and the passage.
